home.title: A place to exhale.
home.subtitle: A private villa on the Samaná Peninsula. Two bedrooms, a private pool, and the Caribbean at your door.
home.interludeTitle: Somewhere between the jungle and the sea.
home.interludeBody: Las Terrenas sits on the north coast of the Samaná Peninsula — a place that somehow missed the resort development that overtook the rest of the island. The beaches are long and uncrowded. The town is small and European in character. The peninsula is covered in jungle right up to the water's edge.
home.escapeTitle: A private corner of the Caribbean.
home.escapeBody: La Dolce Vita is a two-bedroom apartment in a quiet residential complex five minutes from the beach. Private pool, full kitchen, outdoor terrace. Designed for people who travel to actually be somewhere.

about.intro1: A private two-bedroom residence on the Samaná Peninsula, steps from one of the most beautiful beaches in the Dominican Republic. The apartment sits on Ave 27 de Febrero in Las Terrenas — a town that feels like the south of France dropped into the Caribbean.
about.intro2: Two bedrooms, two private bathrooms, a full kitchen, and a private pool shaded by palms. Comfortable enough for a family. Quiet enough for two. The kind of place where a week turns into a longer conversation.
about.address: Ave 27 de Febrero, Apartment 2 · Las Terrenas, Samaná · Dominican Republic
areaFacts: French and Italian expat community — cosmopolitan but Caribbean-relaxed.
Three languages on the street: Dominican Spanish, French, and English.
Food truck park in town, open daily from 4 pm with twelve trucks.
Nearest airport: Samaná El Catey (AZS). Santo Domingo (SDQ) is two hours by road.
Best weather: December through May. Whale watching season January through March.

beaches.name: Playa Punta Popy
beaches.body: The closest beach to the residence. The town beach — calm clear water, a boardwalk lined with cafés and beach bars, and a lively atmosphere most evenings. Good for a morning coffee with your feet in the sand, or a long afternoon with nowhere to be.

beaches.name: Playa Bonita
beaches.body: Widely considered the most beautiful beach in Las Terrenas. Calm turquoise water, white sand, and palm trees that lean into the wind. Boutique hotels and restaurants along the shore. The sunsets here are unhurried and spectacular — the kind that make you stay longer than planned.

beaches.name: Playa Las Ballenas
beaches.body: Quiet and windswept, with an end-of-the-world feeling that the other beaches lack. Best walked at golden hour, when the light turns amber and the beach is mostly empty.

beaches.name: Playa Cosón
beaches.body: Seven kilometres of wild, undeveloped beach — one of the longest in the Dominican Republic. A favourite among surfers and anyone who wants to feel genuinely far from civilisation. Bring water.

beaches.name: Playa Morón
beaches.body: Remote and peaceful, with almost no crowds even in high season. Pristine water, dramatic cliffs nearby, and the kind of silence that's hard to find anywhere on the peninsula.

beaches.name: Playa Rincón
beaches.body: Consistently ranked among the best beaches in the Caribbean — and it earns it. A long arc of white sand backed by coconut palms, with a river at one end and clear Atlantic water. Worth every minute of the drive.

beaches.name: Cayo Levantado
beaches.body: A small island in Samaná Bay — also known as Bacardi Island after a commercial filmed here in the 1970s. Voted one of the world's top 50 beaches. White sand, palm trees leaning over the water, and turquoise you can see straight through to the bottom. Only reachable by ferry from Samaná town.

beaches.name: Las Galeras
beaches.body: A small fishing village at the far tip of the Samaná Peninsula. The drive alone is worth it — winding roads through jungle and hills. Several small beaches within the village, each one more secluded than the last.

excursions.title: The
excursions.subtitle: Eight excursions worth leaving the residence for.

excursions.name: Humpback Whale Watching
excursions.body: Every year, thousands of humpback whales migrate to Samaná Bay to breed — one of the highest concentrations on the planet. You'll hear them before you see them. A local guide boat takes you close enough to watch them breach, and sometimes close enough to feel the spray. There is nothing else like this in the Caribbean.

excursions.name: Salto El Limón
excursions.body: A 40-metre waterfall deep in the jungle hills of Samaná, reached by horseback on a trail through banana trees and bamboo groves. The pool at the base is cold, clear, and completely hidden from the world. About 30 minutes from the residence. One of the best half-days you can spend on the peninsula.

excursions.name: Los Haitises National Park
excursions.body: A vast protected wilderness of mangroves, limestone karst formations, and caves lined with Taíno petroglyphs. Over 230 bird species, including several endemic to the Dominican Republic. Reached by boat through channels of ancient green forest. Bring a camera and a full day.

excursions.name: Playa Rincón Day Trip
excursions.body: Consistently ranked among the top beaches in the Caribbean — and difficult to reach, which is exactly why it stays pristine. Three kilometres of white sand, a river at one end, coconut palms the whole way. Go by boat for the full arrival experience. Bring lunch, or eat at the small local spots on the beach.

excursions.name: Snorkeling & Private Boat Charter
excursions.body: Charter a local boat and pick your own route — hidden coves, shallow reefs, and beaches only accessible by sea. The water off the Samaná Peninsula is clear enough to see coral formations and sea turtles from the surface. Best arranged through a local guide who knows the spots that don't appear on any map.

excursions.name: ATV & Coffee Plantation Tour
excursions.body: Ride ATVs through jungle trails into the hills above Las Terrenas, stopping at local farms where cacao, coffee, and tropical fruit are grown. You'll taste things straight from the tree. A reminder that this island produces some of the finest cacao and coffee in the world, and almost none of it gets exported.

excursions.name: Zipline in the Rainforest
excursions.body: Over two kilometres of zipline cables through the forest canopy above Las Terrenas. The views open up between the trees — ocean on one side, mountains on the other. A good option for families or anyone who wants a rush without going far.

excursions.name: Kitesurfing & Surf Lessons
excursions.body: Playa Cosón and El Portillo both have consistent wind and surf, with local instructors available for all levels. Kitesurfing schools operate year-round with equipment rental included. If you've never tried it, the wide empty beaches here are as good a place as any to start.
